newsitem.title: USA: CoreStates to clear MoneyGram transactions.
newsitem.headline: CoreStates to clear MoneyGram transactions.

text.p: CoreStates Financial Corp. will clear and settle international money transfers for MoneyGram Payment Systems Inc. the two companies said Monday.
A spokeswoman for Philadelpia-based CoreStates said there would be an "incremental impact" on revenue but declined to provide figures.

Warren Bechtel, a spokesman for MoneyGram, said the Mexican bank Banamex will continue in its role as the main paying agent for MoneyGram in Mexico, the biggest part of MoneyGram's foreign money transfer business.
He said the arrangement with CoreStates addresses the need for MoneyGram to have a structure to clear and settle globally as its overseas business grows rapidly.
Bechtel said Lakewood, Colo.-based MoneyGram handled about 5.8 million transactions last year and the number is expected to grow to more than 6 million this year.
The average amount of a MoneyGram transaction is slightly less than $300.

"Because we can offer international customers a tight interbank spread on exchange rates together with a specific currency management system, MoneyGram gains a greater measure of control over its foreign exchange costs and benefits," Harry Hayman, managing director of foreign exchange/institutional sales and consulting at CoreStates Capital Markets, said in a statement announcing the agreement.
MoneyGram, formerly a part of First Data Corp., went public in an initial offering of stock in 1996.
